overview.purpose: High-performance, Redis-backed distributed message queue and job orchestration framework supporting atomic state transitions, token-fenced distributed leasing, parent-child dependency workflows, delayed scheduling, deduplication, and sandboxed child process execution.
overview.architectureType: Redis-backed client-worker queue with token-fenced leasing, Lua-mediated atomic state transitions, mark-and-sweep stall detection, and child process isolation
keyDifferentiators: Atomic Lua-mediated state transitions: All queue state transitions (wait, active, delayed, completed, failed, paused, waiting-children) execute as atomic single-roundtrip Redis Lua scripts, eliminating distributed consensus overhead.

Token-fenced distributed leasing: Workers acquire unique UUID ownership tokens upon dequeue and renew locks via periodic batch heartbeats; state finalization strictly validates the ownership token in Lua before releasing locks.

Parent-child dependency flows: FlowProducer enables tree-structured job DAGs where parent tasks remain in waiting-children state until all child dependencies atomically report completion or handled failure.

Decentralized two-phase mark-and-sweep stall recovery: Workers periodically mark active jobs in a Redis set and sweep unrenewed expired locks back to wait or failed states without requiring a central coordinator.

Sandboxed execution via ChildPool: Isolates long-running, CPU-intensive, or memory-heavy tasks in separate Node.js processes or worker threads with automated lifecycle management and SIGKILL recovery.

transitions.mechanism: Redis Lua script moveToActive-11.lua executes RPOPLPUSH from wait key to active key, sets lock with SET PX NX, sets processedOn and pb fields, increments ats counter, and appends active event to event stream.

evidence.luaOrCodeBehavior: rcall('RPOPLPUSH', waitKey, activeKey); rcall('SET', lockKey, token, 'PX', lockDuration); rcall('HMSET', jobKey, 'processedOn', processedOn); rcall('HINCRBY', jobKey, 'ats', 1); rcall('XADD', eventStreamKey, '*', 'event', 'active')

transitions.mechanism: Redis Lua script moveToFinished-14.lua validates token via removeLock, removes jobId from active list via LREM, adds to completed sorted set via ZADD, updates returnvalue and finishedOn, decrements parent dependencies if parent exists, and emits completed event.

evidence.observation: Validates token match, removes lock, removes jobId from active list via LREM, and transitions job to completed set while notifying parent dependencies.

transitions.mechanism: Redis Lua script moveToDelayed-12.lua validates lock token, removes from active list via LREM, calculates score (timestamp + delay) * 0x1000, inserts into delayed sorted set via ZADD, adds delay marker, and emits delayed event.

evidence.observation: Removes lock, removes from active list, computes 64-bit delayed score timestamp * 0x1000 + sub-priority, and inserts into delayed zset.

guardConditions: Job has no failed children (ZCARD unsuccessfulKey == 0)

evidence.luaOrCodeBehavior: rcall('ZREM', parentWaitingChildrenKey, parentId); rcall('RPUSH', parentWaitKey, parentId); rcall('XADD', parentQueueKey .. ':events', '*', 'event', 'waiting')

transitions.mechanism: Redis Lua script moveStalledJobsToWait-9.lua checks members in stalledKey; if lock key is expired/missing, removes jobId from active list, increments stc counter, moves job to wait list, and emits stalled event.

evidence.observation: 2-phase sweep removes active job without lock, increments stalled counter (stc), re-enqueues into wait list, and emits stalled event.
evidence.luaOrCodeBehavior: if rcall('EXISTS', jobKey .. ':lock') == 0 then rcall('LREM', activeKey, 1, jobId); rcall('HINCRBY', jobKey, 'stc', 1); moveJobToWait(...); rcall('XADD', eventStreamKey, '*', 'event', 'stalled')

evidence.observation: Pops highest-priority job from prioritized sorted set and pushes to active list.
evidence.luaOrCodeBehavior: local result = rcall('ZPOPMIN', prioritizedKey, 1); if #result > 0 then rcall('RPUSH', activeKey, result[1]); return result[1] end

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: Worker process crash or network partition during job processing (Orphaned / Stalled Jobs)
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: Decentralized 2-phase mark-and-sweep: active jobs are added to the stalled set on each check; after stalledInterval, any job in the stalled set whose lock key bull:<qname>:<jobId>:lock has expired (EXISTS == 0) is flagged as stalled.
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: moveStalledJobsToWait-9.lua sweeps the expired job out of the active list, increments the stalled counter stc, and returns it to the wait list (or marks defa failed if stc > maxStalledCount), emitting a stalled stream event.

sourceEvidence.observation: Atomically re-enqueues jobs missing lock keys back to wait list and emits stalled event.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: Deleted scheduler left repeatable child jobs orphaned without ever reaching max stalled threshold.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Added scheduler existence check in moveStalledJobsToWait-9.lua to fail orphaned jobs whose schedulers were deleted.

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Configure stalledInterval and lockDuration according to expected task duration and set maxStalledCount >= 1 to prevent poison-pill infinite crash loops.

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: Extended Node.js event loop lag or GC pause exceeding lock duration (Dual Execution Risk)
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: LockManager fails to renew lock before lockDuration expires; peer worker's stalled checker sweeps the job and assigns it to a second worker.
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: When the original lagging worker finally resumes and attempts moveToCompleted/moveToFailed, moveToFinished-14.lua detects lock mismatch/absence via removeLock and returns error code -6 or -2, rejecting state modification and aborting completion.

sourceEvidence.observation: removeLock returns -6 when lock token differs or -2 when lock key is missing, rejecting completion.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: Event loop block or GC freeze causing lock expiration while job processing continues in memory.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Enforced atomic token-checked lock release inside Lua scripts before any state modification.

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Implement downstream database idempotency tokens / fencing tokens; offload heavy CPU work to sandboxed worker threads using ChildPool.

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: Redis Sentinel failover or abrupt socket disconnect during blocking waitForJob
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: Blocking connection (BZPOPMIN) hangs or enters disconnected state without receiving socket EOF during Sentinel master re-election.
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: Worker's waitForJob catch handler invokes backend.reconnectBlocking() to re-establish the dedicated blocking transport before retrying the dequeue loop.

sourceEvidence.observation: Catches socketless Sentinel disconnects and explicitly calls reconnectBlocking() on the dedicated blocking connection.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: Sentinel failover caused blocking client to become stuck in a disconnected state without recovery.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Added explicit reconnectBlocking() in worker error handling loop.

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Maintain separate Redis connections for blocking commands and standard commands, with automated transport recovery on failover events.

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: Poison-pill task crashing child process in sandboxed execution
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: Child process emits 'exit' event or throws during child.init() / process execution.
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: ChildPool immediately cleans references, invokes SIGKILL, deletes retained child entry, and surfaces the failure to Worker as an unhandled error so the job is marked failed.

sourceEvidence.observation: ChildPool catches initialization/runtime failure, executes SIGKILL, and purges the child instance.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: Failed child initializations remained in the free pool as zombie processes, failing all subsequent jobs.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Purged dead/refused child processes with SIGKILL immediately upon init failure.

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Always isolate untrusted or memory-intensive tasks in sandboxed processes and enforce hard SIGKILL timeouts on unresponsive workers.

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: Redis cluster hash-slot misalignment across multi-key operations
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: Redis cluster returns CROSSSLOT error when executing Lua scripts or multi-key operations spanning different key prefixes.
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: BullMQ encloses all queue key prefixes in Redis hash tags {bull:<qname>} (e.g. {bull:myqueue}:wait, {bull:myqueue}:active), guaranteeing that all keys for a given queue hash to the exact same cluster node.

sourceEvidence.observation: Generates Redis hash tags {prefix:name} for all queue-specific data structures.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: Cluster topology changes and multi-key commands caused slot mismatches when hash tags were not strictly unified.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Enforced uniform hash-tagging across all queue keys and scripts.

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Enforce strict hash-tagging on all queue-related keys in Redis cluster environments.

historicalEvolution.milestoneOrBug: Enforcement of Priority Maximum (2^21 - 1) to Prevent IEEE 754 Float Score Precision Loss
historicalEvolution.rootCause: Redis sorted set scores are 64-bit IEEE double floats with 53 bits of precision. The bit-packing formula (priority * 2^32 + counter % 2^32) exceeded 2^53 - 1 when priority > 2,097,151, causing precision collapse in the low-order counter bits and destroying FIFO ordering among equal-priority jobs.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Enforced PRIORITY_LIMIT = 2^21 - 1 in Job options validation and documentation, ensuring the packed score always remains strictly within the lossless 53-bit integer range.

evidence.observation: Defined export const PRIORITY_LIMIT = 2 ** 21 - 1 and added bounds checking.

historicalEvolution.milestoneOrBug: Dedicated Blocking Client Recovery After Sentinel Failover Disconnect
historicalEvolution.rootCause: During Redis Sentinel failover or abrupt socket disconnections while waiting on BZPOPMIN, the dedicated blocking connection was aborted by the watchdog but left in a disconnected transport state, causing the worker loop to hang or throw unhandled connection errors continuously.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Added explicit backend.reconnectBlocking() recovery logic in the worker's waitForJob error handler to ensure the blocking transport is reconnected before resuming dequeue attempts.

evidence.observation: Added await this.backend.reconnectBlocking() in waitForJob catch block.

historicalEvolution.milestoneOrBug: Purging Zombie Child Processes in ChildPool on Initialization Failure
historicalEvolution.rootCause: When a sandboxed child process or worker thread threw an exception during initialization, the failed process was not killed and remained eligible for reuse, turning into a zombie worker that instantly failed every subsequent job assigned to it.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Added catch block in ChildPool.retain to issue an immediate SIGKILL to the defective child and purge it from the pool before re-throwing the initialization error.

evidence.observation: Wrapped child.init() in try/catch and added this.kill(child, 'SIGKILL') upon failure.

historicalEvolution.milestoneOrBug: Preservation of Custom jobId When Requeueing keepLastIfActive Deduplication Jobs
historicalEvolution.rootCause: When a deduplicated job with keepLastIfActive: true arrived while an active instance was executing, the buffered proto-job failed to preserve the caller's custom jobId, causing the subsequent requeued job to receive an auto-generated numeric ID upon finalization.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Updated storeDeduplicatedNextJob.lua and requeueDeduplicatedJob.lua to serialize and restore the custom jobId across the deduplication lifecycle.

evidence.observation: Extracted and forwarded custom jobId during proto-job promotion in Lua.

historicalEvolution.milestoneOrBug: Bounding Stalled Job Retries for Deleted Schedulers
historicalEvolution.rootCause: Repeatable jobs were unconditionally exempted from maxStalledCount failure. If a scheduler was deleted while one of its child instances was active and stalled, the stalled job was perpetually moved back to wait, resulting in an infinite stall-retry loop.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Added scheduler hash key existence verification in moveStalledJobsToWait-9.lua; if the parent scheduler hash does not exist and stalledCount > maxStalledCount, the job is failed with 'job stalled more than allowable limit'.

evidence.observation: Probed repeatKey:jobSchedulerId existence before deciding whether to exempt stalled job from failure.

unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.claimOrGuarantee: Worker holds exclusive mutual exclusion during task execution.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.contradictionOrBypass: If worker execution blocks or experiences a GC pause longer than lockDuration without renewing the lock, the mark-and-sweep stalled checker reassigns the job to a second worker. While moveToFinished rejects the first worker's eventual completion via token check (-6), both workers execute business logic concurrently in user space against un-fenced external systems (at-least-once dual execution).
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.evidence: The lock token is validated only upon Redis state transition, not during intermediate I/O performed by the worker process.

unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.contradictionOrBypass: While single-queue flow trees are executed atomically via addFlow Lua script, cross-queue flows across Redis cluster instances cannot be executed atomically in a single script due to Redis cluster cross-slot limitations, requiring sequential script executions that are vulnerable to partial tree persistence if the client crashes mid-operation.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.evidence: Cross-queue parent-child linkages in cluster environments span distinct hash slots {bull:queueA} vs {bull:queueB}.

unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.claimOrGuarantee: ChildPool subprocess isolation prevents event loop blockage.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.contradictionOrBypass: While subprocess execution isolates JavaScript CPU execution, large job payload parameters and return values must undergo full JSON serialization/deserialization across the Node.js IPC channel, creating main process event loop micro-stalls and doubling memory consumption under high payload volumes.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.evidence: IPC messages pass through process.send() with structured clone / JSON serialization in the parent process.

boundaryConditions: Synchronous un-yielded CPU computation in Node.js event loop exceeding lockDuration + lockRenewTime causes automatic job stalling and dual execution by peer workers.
Redis Sentinel master failover during multi-command pipeline execution can drop uncommitted pipeline stages, requiring idempotent retry loops.
NTP clock skew between client application nodes and Redis server host can distort scheduled delay scores in delayed sorted sets.
Redis cluster multi-queue flows span distinct hash slots and cannot execute within a single atomic Lua script.
untestedAssumptions: Assumes that user processor functions check AbortSignal or complete within lockDuration without hanging indefinitely on un-instrumented socket I/O.

Assumes that Redis memory is sufficient to store complete job payloads and parent-child dependency sets without triggering Redis maxmemory eviction policies that could silently drop lock keys or job hashes.
Assumes monotonic clock consistency for lock renewal intervals on worker hosts.
acceptedTradeOffs: At-least-once delivery over strict exactly-once processing: Prioritizes throughput and crash recovery over distributed consensus (e.g. 2PC / Raft), requiring downstream handlers to be idempotent.

Lua script atomicity over distributed storage independence: Deeply couples queue semantics to Redis single-threaded script execution, making backend migration to generic SQL or non-Redis stores non-trivial.
Polling/sweeping stall detection over distributed heartbeats: Accepts stalledInterval latency (default 30s) before detecting dead workers to avoid high network heartbeat overhead.
